candidateRootCauses.title: Loading state is re-entered after content has rendered
candidateRootCauses.hypothesis: A data request issued after the first render (for example a refetch triggered by another response) switches the page back into its initial loading state, so the loading placeholder covers content that was already displayed. A shared "loading" flag used for both the initial load and background refreshes is a common cause.

supportingEvidence.note: Loading indicator re-appeared at +887ms while content had been visible since +449ms.
GET http://127.0.0.1:4173/api/products?sort=price started within 150ms of the indicator re-appearing and completed shortly before it was hidden.
GET http://127.0.0.1:4173/api/preferences completed immediately before the indicator re-appeared (possible trigger).

confidence.explanation: The visual re-entry is directly observed in 2 document load(s), and every episode coincides with an API request that starts as the indicator appears and completes as it disappears. This is a consistent temporal correlation; it has not been confirmed by changing request timing, so it is not rated high.

suggestedExperiments: Delay the response that precedes the re-appearance (e.g. in a local mock) and check whether the flicker moves with it; this tests causation rather than correlation.
Inspect the code path handling that response for a state update that resets the page-level loading flag or replaces content with the placeholder.
Reload the page several times (reproduce_issue with multiple reload steps) to measure how often the re-appearance occurs.
